reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown take Deuteronomy 5:4's face to face as the directness of Yahweh's speech, not a visible form, consistent with 4:12's denial that any shape was seen.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats Deuteronomy 1-4 and 5-11 as two separately composed historical introductions later joined to the law-book, a seam this face-to-face/no-form clash instances.

quotes.text: Deuteronomy, when it was first discovered, was a pure law-book. … The two historical introductions, chapter i.-iv. and chapter v.-xi. were added later, as well as the appendices, chapter xxviii. seq.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on Deuteronomy's two separately-added historical introductions (chs. 1-4 and 5-11).
